title: UN week 2026: AI took center stage, but no new rules or money
question: What did the United Nations high-level week actually authorize, fund or put into operation, and what remained a speech, proposal or scheduled next step?
bluf: At the 2026 UN General Assembly week, AI and tokenization got far more attention and a UN AI-strategy method was launched, but nothing crossed into an adopted rule, a funded program or an operating system.
evidence_cutoff_note: The September 22 late-release wave preserves twenty newly posted Day One formal statements and reconciles them with the complete official-caption session version. Twenty-three of 31 country pages expose statement PDFs; the twenty additions contain 202 pages, all rendered and visually inspected. At 23:16 EDT, all eight no-PDF country pages exposed downloadable UN AI transcripts explicitly marked auto-generated and potentially erroneous. The eight files are preserved with hashes. Token comparison against the final-session captions yields two exact matches and 99.41-99.97 per cent similarity for the other six, with only clip-boundary spill or two Qatar name normalizations; the downloads are therefore the same caption family, not independent corroboration. Separate local official-audio transcripts remain genuinely independent passes for the United States and United Kingdom. By 23:25 EDT, the official UN WebTV event objects for General Debate Day Two, both Right to Development parts and the climate/just-transition event were published and fixed in the capture contract. The proved capture route and later baseline captures keep event-object publication separate from delivery. A 00:18 comparison found no WebTV state change. At 00:21, the official Day Two view exposed 21 morning and 16 afternoon schedule cards but zero country-page links; a direct Syrian Arab Republic page request returned to the General Debate landing page. At 00:44, the Right to Development legal/process baseline added eight primary UN PDFs totaling 121 rendered and visually inspected pages. It distinguishes the adopted non-treaty Declaration and operating mandate machinery from the unadopted covenant; records the 29–13–5 HRC transmission, continuing divergent Working Group views, the 28–14–5 HRC continuation resolution and the 127–23–32 current General Assembly resolution; and preserves the unreached negotiation, adoption, consent, entry-into-force, Conference and implementation-mechanism gates. At 01:04, another four-object WebTV comparison remained unchanged, the eight Day One no-PDF pages still exposed no speaker-authorized statement, and the first Day Two country route still redirected to the landing page. At 01:30, the rendered 21-page UN Journal and six structured Journal responses fixed four formal General Assembly meeting UUIDs, their room/time/agenda and WebTV joins, plus four exposed eStatements routes whose underlying agenda-view and speaker-view arrays were still empty. The 7th and 8th plenaries share one WebTV entry and therefore require meeting-aware transcript segmentation. At 01:47, the Right to Development public data changed: Costa Rica moved from slot 36 to 98 and from Foreign Minister Manuel Tovar-Rivera to Vice Minister of Multilateral Affairs Adriana Bolaños Argueta; sixty-two intervening entities shifted forward one slot, while the entity set, approvals and ready/done/skip totals remained fixed. A versioned raw source, complete projection and generated entity-level delta preserve the change without overwriting the first list. A generic manifest/hash-verified projection tool now distinguishes live rolling captions from completed de-duplicated assets and withholds speaker headings until a separate official interval map exists. Prepared text remains subordinate to the recording for delivery. Release, retrieval, source version, prepared text, delivery, interpretation, captioning, candidacy, negotiation, adoption, enactment, funding, entry into force, deployment and operation retain distinct clocks. At 02:17, the preserved official General Debate e-Speakers feed confirmed the earlier public roster exactly at twenty-one approved morning and sixteen approved afternoon speakers. Italy and Uzbekistan exist only as unapproved afternoon raw records; all approved entries remain zero ready, zero done, zero skipped and without end-time values. A byte-level return found all twenty-three preserved Day One statement PDFs unchanged, the eight other country pages still without a speaker-authorized PDF, and the 02:12 four-object WebTV comparison unchanged. At 02:32, the reusable official Journal API comparator found no source-state change across the four formal meeting records: all remained open, not cancelled and at zero statements, documents and summaries. At 03:18, the country-summary register contract fixed one compact summary per delivered address, explicit pending rows during live work and reasoned-only escalation. At 03:28, the General Debate feed remained byte-identical to the 02:17 source, all four WebTV objects remained at zero duration with no audio or captions, all four Journal records remained open and empty, the Syria statement region remained asset-empty, and all 37 schedule cards still exposed no country hrefs or node IDs. At 04:52, all 37 explicitly selected Day Two schedule rows remained unlinked, Syria remained asset-empty and the home-page live chrome still described Day One; the stale carousel and closed banner do not prove Day Two delivery. At 05:13, a 35-page primary-source Syria baseline separated eight representation, authority, sanctions, control, normalization and reconstruction clocks and fixed a presumptive deep-review disposition without advancing the scheduled speech to delivery. At 05:40, a 25-page Iran baseline corrected the prior no-agreement line and separated safeguards, verification, disputed UN sanctions, U.S. pressure, the incomplete Islamabad framework and force clocks. At 06:00, the roster, four WebTV objects and four Journal records remained unchanged. At 06:04, a 21-page Argentina baseline joined the Day One reply to the June C-24 decision and September Law 26.659 machinery while preserving opened proceedings, final sanctions, foreign effect, negotiation and title as separate states.
use_note: Use for the September 18–29 UNGA81 event window, its research stack and the connected UN authority/U.S.-role architecture. The Day Two primary-source preflight and watchboard is the current read-first route; every listed intervention remains scheduled until reconciled against the official delivered record. For the Right to Development meeting, use the declaration/covenant/implementation baseline to keep support for the right, support for the 1986 Declaration, support for a binding instrument and support for the present draft distinct; no treaty adoption, signature, consent, entry into force, Conference of States Parties or implementation mechanism is established. Use every transcript only as navigation into the controlling official video or original audio, and replay exact passages before publication. Use the proved WebTV capture method to preserve versioned in-progress and final caption/audio records without treating source access as transcript accuracy or delivery. For Japan, use the UN-hosted provisional translation for prepared wording and the final video for delivered wording. The September 22 speech audit controls the United States-Brazil interpretation and the September 21 audit controls Digital Cooperation Day. Do not treat a side-event agenda, launch, speech, threat, meeting, signature, final draft, scientific report, proposed fund or closed design session as an adopted or operating object. Follow later outcomes to the UN Journal, official meeting pages, national legal instruments and adopted document records while preserving release, retrieval, source-version, prepared-text, delivery, enactment, entry-into-force and operation times.

availability_semantics.public_reading: The public site contains both the original public view and a crawler-friendly static HTML reading edition. public_full_text is true.
availability_semantics.public_machine_data: The public site contains the complete positively selected structured dataset. public_full_text is true; reading_url and data_url identify the canonical JSON object.
availability_semantics.private_library_metadata: The governed private Research Library contains the material, but the public site exposes only safe title, role and state metadata. public_full_text is false and access_state is private_by_design. Do not infer its contents.

retrieval_instructions: Open full_text_url for the package before treating a summary as the underlying research.
For a public reading, prefer reading_url. For public_machine_data, open data_url and preserve its schema_version, data_as_of, scope_boundary and evidence vocabulary.
A failure to retrieve public_full_text is an access or crawler problem, not a private-by-design signal.
For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
